'''Adam Sebastian Genevieve Curtis''' (3 January 1934 &ndash; 8 August 2017) was a British cell biologist who researched [[cell adhesion]] and [[contact inhibition]]. He worked at the [[University of Glasgow]] from 1967 until he became a professor [[emeritus]] in 2004. He was president of the [[Society for Experimental Biology]] from 1993 to 1995 and an elected fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] and [[Royal Society of Biology]].

==Early life and education==
Adam Sebastian Genevieve Curtis was born on 3 January 1934 in London, at the [[South London Hospital for Women and Children]].<ref name="story">{{cite web| url=https://universitystory.gla.ac.uk/biography/?id=WH1388&type=P| title=Adam Curtis| website=The University of Glasgow Story| access-date=9 April 2021| year=2017| archive-date=21 April 2021| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421025208/https://universitystory.gla.ac.uk/biography/?id=WH1388&type=P| url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="part 1">{{cite web| url=https://sounds.bl.uk/Oral-history/Science/021M-C1379X0114XX-0001V0| title=Curtis, Adam (1 of 15) An Oral History of British Science| website=British Library Sounds| year=2014| access-date=9 April 2021| archive-date=7 August 2020| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807180503/https://sounds.bl.uk/Oral-history/Science/021M-C1379X0114XX-0001V0| url-status=dead}}</ref> His father, Herbert Lewis Curtis, was an architect who served in World War I by surveying aerial photographs. His mother, Nora Patricia {{nee|Stevens}} was born in Ireland and studied painting at [[Slade School of Fine Art]].<ref name="part 1"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://suffolkartists.co.uk/index.cgi?choice=painter&pid=4214| title=CURTIS, Nora Patricia| website=Suffolk Artists| access-date=9 April 2021}}</ref>

He initially planned on studying [[geology]] and applied to [[King's College, Cambridge|King's College]] and [[University of Cambridge]]. He decided to attend Cambridge and study biology instead of geology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sounds.bl.uk/Oral-history/Science/021M-C1379X0114XX-0003V0|title=Curtis, Adam (3 of 15) An Oral History of British Science|website=British Library Sounds|year=2014|access-date=9 April 2021|archive-date=20 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120040214/https://sounds.bl.uk/Oral-history/Science/021M-C1379X0114XX-0003V0|url-status=dead}}</ref> He attended the [[University of Edinburgh]] for his PhD, studying in its Institute of Animal Genetics under advisors [[C. H. Waddington]] and Geoffrey Selman.<ref name="phd">
{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last=Curtis |first=A.S.G. |date=1957 |title=Some biological studies of developmental processes |chapter= |publisher= |docket= |hdl=1842/13532 |oclc=606111564 |url=https://era.ed.ac.uk/handle/1842/13532 |access-date=}}
</ref><ref name="Curtis">{{Cite journal|last1=Centre for Cell Engineering, University of Glasgow, Scotland|last2=Curtis|first2=Asg|date=2004-10-22|title=Small is beautiful but smaller is the aim: Review of a life of research|journal=European Cells and Materials|volume=8|pages=27–36|doi=10.22203/eCM.v008a04|pmid=15508070|doi-access=free}}</ref> He then returned to London to complete a post-doctoral research appointment with [[Michael Abercrombie]], where he researched [[contact inhibition]], the mechanisms by which cells stop moving upon contact with another body.<ref name="Curtis"/><ref name="SEB"/>

==Career==
In 1962, he became a lecturer of zoology at [[University College London]]. In 1967, he began working in the newly established Department of Cell Biology at the [[University of Glasgow]], where he thus became the first professor of cell biology in the UK.<ref name="SEB"/> In 1997, he was a co-founder of the Centre for Cell Engineering at the University of Glasgow along with Chris Wilkinson.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://glasgow.thecemi.org/about-us/| title=About Us| website=The University of Glasgow Centre for the Cellular Microenvironment| date=9 May 2017| access-date=9 April 2021}}</ref> He also helped found the Tissue and Cell Engineering Society UK and served as its president from 2001 to 2003.<ref name="SEB"/>

Curtis's observations of cell movement across a surface lead to novel experimentation with using nanovibrations to direct the behavior of [[stem cell]]s, which was called "nanokicking".<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.gla.ac.uk/research/az/thecemi/blog/nanokickingstemcellstogrownewbone/| title=NANOKICKING STEM CELLS TO GROW NEW BONE| website=THE CENTRE FOR THE CELLULAR MICROENVIRONMENT (THE CEMI)| access-date=9 April 2021| date=13 September 2017| first=P. Monica| last=Tsimbouri| archive-date=1 August 2021| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210801041326/https://www.gla.ac.uk/research/az/thecemi/blog/nanokickingstemcellstogrownewbone/| url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2004 he retired, becoming a professor [[emeritus]].<ref name="SEB"/> Some of the doctoral students that he advised included [[Cheryll Tickle]] and [[Richard B. Gallagher]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://dev.biologists.org/content/develop/143/7/1057.full.pdf| doi=10.1242/dev.136671| title=An interview with Cheryll Tickle| year=2016| last1=Vicente| first1=Catarina| journal=Development| volume=143| issue=7| pages=1057–1059| pmid=27048683| s2cid=21143007| doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis| last1=Gallagher| first1=Richard B.|url=http://theses.gla.ac.uk/71772/| title=Studies on cell adhesion in relation to immune responses| website=University of Glasgow| date=1984| doi=10.5525/gla.thesis.71772| access-date=9 April 2021| type=PhD}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
In 1972 he was awarded the Cuvier Medal by the [[Zoological Society of France]]. He was an elected fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]], the [[Royal Society of Biology]], and of Biomaterials Science and Engineering.<ref name="story"/> He served as the president of the [[Society for Experimental Biology]] from 1993 to 1995.<ref name="SEB">{{cite web| url=https://www.sebiology.org/publications/magazine/article/autumn-2017/in-remembrance-of-adam-curtis| title=IN REMEMBRANCE OF ADAM CURTIS| website=Society of Experimental Biology| access-date=9 April 2017| year=2017| first=Mathis| last=Riehle| archive-date=21 July 2020| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200721005146/https://www.sebiology.org/publications/magazine/article/autumn-2017/in-remembrance-of-adam-curtis| url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
He married Ann Curtis in 1958; they had met at the University of Edinburgh. They had two daughters together, [[Penelope Curtis]] and Susanna. He died on 8 August 2017.<ref name="story"/>
